title: The Crab and the Fox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Crab once left the sea-shore and went and settled in a meadow some way inland, which looked very nice and green and seemed likely to be a good place to feed in. But a hungry Fox came along and spied the Crab and caught him. Just as he was going to be eaten up, the Crab said, "This is just what I deserve; for I had no business to leave my natural home by the sea and settle here as though I belonged to the land."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Crab originally live?
options: In a shaded forest
Beside a quiet river
By the sea-shore
In a rocky cave

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Crab settle in the meadow?
options: It looked very nice and green and seemed a good place to feed
It was closer to his family
It offered better protection from predators
He was chased there by another Crab

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who catches the Crab in the meadow?
options: A passing hawk
A farmer working the field
Another Crab from the shore
A hungry Fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crab say just before being eaten?
options: That the Fox should let him go
That this is just what he deserves
That he will never make this mistake again
That the meadow was not worth the risk

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crab say he had no business doing?
options: Wandering so far from his family
Trusting a stranger he had just met
Leaving his natural home by the sea to settle on land
Ignoring the warnings of other crabs

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Crab believe his fate is deserved?
options: He recognizes that leaving his natural environment put him in danger he could have avoided
He believes the Fox has more right to eat him than any other animal
He thinks all crabs are eventually caught no matter where they live
He believes he provoked the Fox somehow before being caught

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what made the meadow seem like a good choice at first?
options: It was recommended by another crab who lived there
It was closer to fresh water than the shore
It had fewer foxes than the area near the sea
Its pleasant, green appearance suggested it would be safe and full of food

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "spied" mean in "spied the Crab"?
options: Warned about
Caught sight of
Chased away
Befriended quietly

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Crab had "no business" doing something?
options: He had no financial means to do it
He had no time available to do it
He had no good reason or right to do it
He had no one to help him do it

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Straying from what suits your own nature can bring trouble upon you
Foxes are always more dangerous than they appear
Meadows are unsafe for any creature that lives near the sea
Crabs should never trust the appearance of a new place

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how far from the sea does the Crab settle?
options: Just a few steps from the shore
Across a wide river
At the edge of a cliff
Some way inland

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crab say about where he truly belongs?
options: That he belongs wherever food is plentiful
That he belongs by the sea, not on the land
That he belongs with other crabs of his kind
That he no longer knows where he belongs

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition is the Fox in when he finds the Crab?
options: Injured
Lost
Hungry
Frightened

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why doesn't the Crab blame the Fox for what happens to him?
options: He accepts that his own choice to leave his natural home led to his misfortune
He does not realize the Fox is responsible for catching him
He believes the Fox was simply following orders from another animal
He thinks all foxes act the same way regardless of the situation

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what warning does the Crab's fate offer to other creatures?
options: Meadows are always more dangerous than the sea-shore
Foxes only hunt creatures that do not belong in their territory
Crabs should always travel with a companion for safety
Leaving the environment suited to your nature can expose you to unexpected danger

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "lot" mean in the closing line "Be content with your lot"?
options: A piece of land for building
One's own circumstances or situation in life
A large quantity of something
A game of chance

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Crab outwits a Fox and escapes back to the sea
A Fox warns the Crab to return to the sea before it is too late
A Crab is caught by a Fox after leaving the sea for a meadow, and accepts the outcome as his own fault
A Crab convinces the Fox to spare his life
